rationale: This is a deployment-configuration-only artifact (Docker Compose + shell scripts + Selenoid browser config + GitHub issue templates) for the Healenium self-healing framework. It contains zero application source code, zero test files, and zero architecture/design documents. The repo originates from a fork of Healenium, wired to qosha1/healing-playwright remote, but no Playwright-specific code is present. All files orchestrate external Docker images (hlm-backend:3.4.8, hlm-proxy:2.1.6, hlm-selector-imitator:1.6, postgres:15.5-alpine, selenium/node-*). The README describes Healenium as an open-source self-healing library for automated Selenium testing (README line 19-23) that acts as a proxy between client and Selenium server, using machine learning to heal test failures from UI changes. No evidence connects it to a structured laptop-spec extraction pipeline. Tier D reflects that this is a config-only deployment artifact, not source that can be directly integrated.
limitations: Repository contains no application source code -- it is purely Docker Compose orchestration and shell scripts
No test files of any kind exist in the repository
No architecture or design documents present
No evidence of integration with any laptop-spec extraction pipeline

The repository is a shallow clone/fork of Healenium's deployment configuration; Healenium's actual self-healing logic lives in separate upstream repositories (healenium-backend, healenium-proxy, healenium-selector-imitator)
No Playwright-specific code despite the remote pointing to 'healing-playwright'
No CI/CD pipeline configuration beyond GitHub issue templates
License is Apache 2.0 (LICENSE file) but no SPDX identifiers in source since there is no source code
